summary.text: A 44-year-old Japanese woman with stage IIIc ovarian cancer and endometrial cancer underwent surgery to remove the ovarian and surrounding lymph nodes, followed 15 days later by platinum-based chemotherapy, first with paclitaxel and carboplatin. Bevacizumab was added from the second to sixth course and then continued alone, last given at the 21st course. Her gynecologist suggested a dental visit for gingival pain and bleeding on brushing.

General adverse effects and a strange gingival feeling appeared on the third day after the first injection and emerged similarly with docetaxel and carboplatin in the third course. The general effects faded but the oral problem worsened, with gingival bleeding and swelling about a week after every bevacizumab injection, which the authors state bevacizumab induced. She had no hypertension, proteinuria, thrombosis, epistaxis or gastrointestinal perforation.

At her first dental visit, on the day of the 11th course, examination showed grade 2-3 gingival swelling, edematous gingiva with serous hemorrhage, a Plaque Control Record of 82.1%, probing depths generally 4 mm or more with bleeding at most deep sites, and no extensive mucositis or xerostomia. Fear of pain and bleeding had kept her from brushing, and poor oral hygiene worsened the symptoms. She received oral hygiene instruction, supragingival PMTC and soft brushing.

Bevacizumab alone continued every 3 weeks with regular dental visits, evaluations and PMTC; gingival symptoms and fear of bleeding gradually decreased. The Gingival Index, PCR and CEA decreased after the first dental visit; CEA rose after the 18th course and returned to the reference range 1 year later, CA19-9 and CA125 stayed in range, and no recurrence was detected. Four weeks after chemotherapy ended, edematous gingiva persisted around the lower left second molar.

ambiguities.issue: The third course is called a docetaxel and carboplatin combination, while the regimen of paclitaxel and carboplatin is described as repeated six times; the source does not say whether paclitaxel was replaced by docetaxel in the third course.

evidence.quote: Anticancer drugs selected first were paclitaxel and carboplatin as a combination regimen. This administration was repeated six times approximately every 3 weeks.
Although a combination regimen of docetaxel and carboplatin was administrated only in the third course, general adverse effects emerged similarly.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide whether paclitaxel was given in the third course, how many paclitaxel courses were given, or why docetaxel was named; the six-times count is not asserted for paclitaxel.

ambiguities.issue: The "first injection" of the adverse-effect sentence does not name the drug; bevacizumab was first given with the second course, so the anchor could be a chemotherapy or a bevacizumab injection.

evidence.quote: On the third day after the first injection, general adverse effects, which were urticarial, flare, and swelling in part, emerged, and she had strange feeling around the gingiva as an oral adverse effect as well.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not name the drug or course that caused the general adverse effects.

ambiguities.issue: The first dental clinic visit in the opening sentence and the first dental office visit on the day of the 11th course are presumably the same visit but the source does not say so; they are kept as separate events without an ordering relation.

evidence.quote: A 44‐year‐old Japanese woman visited the dental clinic office of the Oral Care Center in Kagoshima University Hospital according to a suggestion by her gynecologist.
On the day of the 11th course of chemotherapy, which was the sixth course of only bevacizumab, the patient visited a dental office for the first time and complained about the oral disorder (Fig. 1).

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge the two visits or assign the chief complaint a date.

ambiguities.issue: The authors assert without hedging that bevacizumab induced the gingival inflammation ("certainly induced"; "induced by administration of bevacizumab"), recorded as a bevacizumab adverse effect. The same report states that poor oral hygiene made the symptoms worse and that the patient was told the symptoms derived from insufficient cleaning and oral contamination as well as the chemotherapy itself; the plaque-plus-mucositis synergy is only hedged ("It is possible").

evidence.quote: In conclusion, the prescription of bevacizumab certainly induced gingival inflammation including swelling, bleeding, and pain during chemotherapy in a patient diagnosed with ovarian cancer and endometrial cancer.
Moreover, poor oral hygiene made the symptoms worse.

It is possible that accumulation of dental plaque, derived from impossibility of toothbrushing, as well as mucositis located at gingiva associated with bevacizumab, could induce severe inflammation in a synergistic manner.
We informed her that the gingival symptoms were derived from insufficient cleaning and bad oral contamination as well as the chemotherapy itself, primarily.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record bevacizumab as the sole cause or the hedged plaque synergy as an asserted cause.

ambiguities.issue: The anchor of "1 year later" for the CEA value returning to the reference range is not named in the sentence; it follows an increase after the 18th course.

evidence.quote: Although CEA increased gradually after the 18th course, the value returned to the reference range 1 year later (CEA: ≤5.0 ng/mL), and recurrence of the cancer was not detected.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a calendar date or a named anchor to the 1-year interval.

ambiguities.issue: The CA19-9 reference interval is printed with the label "CA19-1" in the source (print artefact); it is read as the CA19-9 interval because the same sentence names CA19-9 and CA125.

evidence.quote: Values of CA19‐9 and CA125 were within a reference range during whole chemotherapy (CA19–1: ≤37.0 U/mL; CA125: ≤35.0 U/mL).

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer a separate marker named CA19-1.

ambiguities.issue: The hemorrhage is called "serious" in the Figure 1 caption and "serous" in the text and Figure 2 caption; treated as a print variation.

evidence.quote: Arrows denote edematous gingiva associated with serious hemorrhage.
edematous gingiva associated with serous hemorrhage was detected in many parts

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record two different findings.

ambiguities.issue: Bevacizumab-alone counts do not reconcile arithmetically: an additional 16 injections after the second to sixth course (21 prescriptions in total), the 11th course called the sixth course of only bevacizumab, an additional 10 courses after the first dental visit, and the 21st course printed as the last administration. Arithmetic-only mismatch, not a source conflict.
